bindings.description: Single focal shop arrangement concerning the respondent tenant and his son Arun Sood, whose Sood Store business was operated from the premises. Petitioners allege subletting and exclusive use by Arun; the respondent denies disposition and asserts continued possession, control and business activity alongside his son. General assignment and exclusive-subtenant allegations concerning the same shop are retained without assuming their unidentified recipients are legally identical to Arun.

bindings.identity_reason: The restored narrative expressly identifies the respondent tenant, his son Arun Sood and the tenanted shop in the petitioners' subletting allegation. The respondent's account independently refers to his son Arun Sood, the son's presence in the premises and their business activity. The telephone and bank evidence also identifies Arun as the respondent's son. This establishes the focal father-son shop arrangement. The unnamed assignee and generic exclusively possessing subtenant in the earlier pleading are not thereby established as Arun, and the variant business names are not automatically equated as legal entities.

Its appellate-review context does not make the underlying Section 14(1)(b) tests inapplicable. The unresolved date, consent and legal-possession questions concern specific statutory propositions rather than overall scope. The three disposition routes remain distinct.

original_identity_scope.identity_reason: The respondent-to-Arun Sood relationship and the shop are explicitly identified, and the restored passage supports one focal father-son arrangement. M/s Sood Store and Sood Stores appear as connected business-name descriptions, including one bank account attributed to Arun, but the material does not establish that the differently rendered names are the same legal entity. These unresolved identities do not negate the established respondent-Arun pairing.

bindings.dependency_review_reason: Change the proposed global unresolved identity status to established for the expressly identified respondent-Arun-shop arrangement. Preserve narrower unidentified assignee and exclusive-possessor connections, the missing disposition date and written-consent evidence, and all substantive distinctions between business use, physical occupation and legal possession.

coverage_limits: Only one focal respondent-Arun Sood shop arrangement is proposed. Opposing accounts of that same arrangement are preserved together instead of becoming separate bindings.
The earlier generic assignment and exclusive-subtenant allegations are retained in the same focal record with unknown recipient objects. Their identity with Arun Sood is not presumed.

The respondent admits his son's presence, and the supplied narrative describes simultaneous business activity. These facts support discussion of user and possession distinctions but do not establish legal ouster.
Photographs, telephone-connection evidence and bank-account evidence are judgment-described records, not independently inspected underlying exhibits.
The official-witness description connects a telephone connection to Arun Sood and a Sood Stores bank account to Arun. Neither fact alone determines possession rights.
The date of the alleged disposition is absent. The rent-agreement date is a different event.
Written landlord consent remains unresolved. A contractual restriction does not independently establish the absence of later written consent.
The supplied law does not give a burden allocation, proof standard, burden shift or evidentiary presumption.
All eleven old links and all five original combination limitations have been retained and assigned by restricted use.
No test labels, composite claim satisfaction or eviction outcome are predicted.
